title: Your First Shift
blurb: Join the Four West team for one shift, from morning handover to evening report.

endings.headline: A strong first shift
endings.message: You checked, asked and kept the team informed.
endings.subline: Keep building your skills. Later levels are not built yet.

endings.headline: Try the shift again
endings.message: Use the feedback to choose a safer next step.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Each scored decision adds or removes 6. Reach 85 to pass.

ladderBranches.label: Leadership path
ladderBranches.roles: Director of Nursing → Chief Nursing Officer

preGame.ladderNote: Titles and paths vary by employer. Later levels are planned.

screens.heading: Care, check and communicate.
screens.body: Nurses check patients, give care and tell the team when something changes.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Welcome to Riverbend.
beats.body: Your first shift starts on Four West.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A floor with a view.
beats.body: You will work beside Rosa, an experienced nurse.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: You are part of a team.
beats.body: Ask for help when you need it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Meet Rosa.
beats.body: She will guide you and check your work today.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Your shift is starting. What should you do first?

choices.label: Get an update from the night nurse.
choices.why: The handover tells you what changed and what still needs doing.

choices.label: Begin giving medicine alone.
choices.why: Get the handover and work with your supervising nurse first.

choices.label: Wait without speaking to anyone.
choices.why: Ask for the update so you can begin with the team.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A useful update.
beats.body: You know which patients need a closer check.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: At the bedside.
beats.body: Rosa checks the patient before starting care.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Two checks.
beats.body: Use the patient’s name and date of birth to check who they are.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Which two details help confirm a patient’s identity?

choices.label: Their name and date of birth.
choices.why: These identify the person. Follow the hospital’s approved identity-check process.

choices.label: Their room and bed number.
choices.why: Rooms and beds can change. They do not identify the person.

choices.label: Their blanket and gown color.
choices.why: Clothes and bedding do not identify a patient.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Write what happened.
beats.body: A clear note helps the next nurse understand the change.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Keep records private.
beats.body: Open records only when needed for your care duties.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The floor gets busy.
beats.body: Rosa asks you to stay alert for changes.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: A patient suddenly struggles to breathe. What should you do?

choices.label: Call Rosa and the care team for help now.
choices.why: A sudden change needs prompt attention from the care team.

choices.label: Wait until the next routine check.
choices.why: Do not delay telling the care team about a sudden change.

choices.label: Only add a note for later.
choices.why: Writing a note does not bring immediate help.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Ask when unsure.
beats.body: Rosa gives you an instruction you do not understand.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: You do not understand Rosa’s instruction. What should you say?

choices.label: Please explain before I start.
choices.why: Ask before acting when an instruction is unclear.

choices.label: I will guess what you mean.
choices.why: Guessing can put a patient at risk.

choices.label: I will keep quiet.
choices.why: Rosa needs to know when you need help.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Morning checkpoint.
beats.body: Rosa reviews your first four decisions.

intro.line: Arjun and Samira check your work.

pass.title: A strong first pass.
pass.body: Keep going. The next task is ready.

fail.title: You can recover.
fail.body: Use the feedback on your next task.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The afternoon begins.
beats.body: Denise will review your notes. Rosa stays available to help.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Meet Denise.
beats.body: The nurse manager wants notes the whole team can follow.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A note needs a check.
beats.body: Denise asks you to spot a clear mistake.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Which note needs a time correction?

choices.label: Medicine given tomorrow.
choices.why: A completed action cannot have happened tomorrow. Check the record before changing it.

choices.label: Patient walked at 1 p.m.
choices.why: This is a clear time for a completed action.

choices.label: Family called at noon.
choices.why: This is a clear time for a completed action.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Meet Tyler.
beats.body: The other new nurse is eager to impress the team.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Tyler takes credit for your report in a meeting. What should you do?

choices.label: Speak with Rosa calmly after the meeting.
choices.why: Rosa can help clarify the record without disrupting the meeting.

choices.label: Shout over Tyler.
choices.why: A public argument distracts the team from patient care.

choices.label: Change the patient record to criticize him.
choices.why: Patient records are for care, not a dispute with a colleague.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you skipped a check or missed a chance to tell the team

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Room 12 needs help.
beats.body: Your patient suddenly seems confused and is breathing fast.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Pick two updates the evening nurse needs.

cards.label: Room 12’s breathing changed and the team responded.
Room 9 still needs test results checked.
You liked the view from the staff lounge.

beats.whenRight: Share important changes and unfinished care tasks.
beats.whenWrong: Focus on changes and care still due.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you left out an important handover update

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your shift is complete.
beats.body: The team reviews what you did well and what needs work.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Your first-shift review.
beats.body: See the result of your seven decisions.
